title: Sidecar observation errors can bypass provider and watchdog cleanup

significance.impact: An I/O or projection error can leave an active provider and its watchdog behind.
significance.exposure: run_bounded executions observing provider sidecars, including providers that close stdout/stderr before continuing work.
significance.detectability: The caller receives an observation exception, but that exception did not establish termination.
significance.systemic_implication: Process ownership must wrap all fallible observation, thread setup, and teardown paths; an observer must not be able to skip the owner finalizer.
significance.recovery: The local process boundary is repairable. A returned cancellation cannot roll back already performed actions; no historical provider-side effect was established by these fixtures.
significance.rationale: A shared lifecycle invariant fails under specific descendant or observation conditions. The observed scope warrants a transport-wide repair and regressions, not a claim of arbitrary process containment.

confidence.basis: Independent source inspection followed by real-process pre-fix reproduction at the intended liveness assertions.

evidence.observation: Both a directory-read failure and a planted sidecar-projection failure occurred after the provider closed its output pipes; the provider or watchdog was still running when the caller received the error.
139 affected tests passed after the ownership/idempotence repair; these are source tests, not installed native permission qualification.

claim.failure_mode: The loop catches only KeyboardInterrupt; its finally repeats a fallible sidecar refresh before stopping the watchdog, with no unconditional group cleanup.
claim.downstream_consequence: Failed source/progress observation can be reported while provider work continues and recovery has no reliable stopped boundary.

counterevidence.observation: The existing retained-output-pipe and parent-death checks exercise different paths and passed; they did not reject these five reproduced failures.

proof_limits: Same-group, same-user local processes only; detached sessions and hostile privilege changes are not contained by a process group.
No native provider action, installed-runtime qualification, or recovery/cancellation acknowledgement has been proven.

containment: Use an outer process-ownership context; stop the group before draining after observation errors and do not repeat the failed sidecar read.

remediation.description: Use an outer process-ownership context; stop the group before draining after observation errors and do not repeat the failed sidecar read.
Independently review the repaired lifecycle and exercise its installed approval/recovery consumers before claiming E1 closure.

required: Preserve all five pre-fix assertion rejections as permanent real-process regressions.
An independent reviewer must assess the repaired source and outstanding lifecycle conditions.
